questions.question: Explain four reasons why water heats up and cools down more slowly than land.
questions.expected_answer: First, water has a high specific heat capacity, needing about four times as much energy as dry soil to raise its temperature by one degree. Second, water is transparent, so sunlight penetrates several metres and its heat is spread through a large volume, while land absorbs heat in its top few centimetres. Third, waves, currents and mixing move heat into a deep layer. Fourth, some energy at the surface is used for evaporation rather than raising temperature. So the sea stores heat like a storage heater: cooler than land in summer and by day, warmer in winter and at night, moderating coastal temperatures.

questions.question: Compare the temperatures of Johannesburg and Cape Town in July and explain the difference using distance from the sea.
questions.expected_answer: In July Johannesburg's average maximum is about 17 °C and minimum about 4 °C, a daily range of 13 °C; Cape Town's maximum is about 18 °C and minimum about 7 °C, a range of 11 °C. Johannesburg is about 500 km inland: there is no sea to release stored warmth at night, and its dry, clear winter air with low humidity lets heat escape quickly into space, so nights are cold and frost is common. Cape Town lies beside the ocean, which cools slowly and releases warmth, and its moister air keeps nights milder, so frost is very rare. The comparison is complicated because Johannesburg is about 1 750 m higher and at a lower latitude, so not all differences are due to the sea.

questions.question: Using examples, explain the difference between maritime and continental climates.
questions.expected_answer: A maritime climate, near the sea, has mild winters, cool summers and small daily and annual ranges because the sea moderates temperature; a continental climate, far inland, has hot summers or days, cold winters or nights, and large ranges. Example: at about 50 degrees north, Vancouver on the coast has a January mean of about 4 °C and July about 18 °C, a range of 14 °C, while Winnipeg inland has about minus 16 °C and 20 °C, a range of 36 °C. Yakutsk in Siberia has a range of over 50 °C. In South Africa, Upington and Bloemfontein inland have hot days and frosty nights, while Durban and Gqeberha on the coast are milder.
